answer: Slot-lock deposits price block rights per river slot: a summit auction before each slot sells it to the highest refundable depositor. Honest agents bid only for slots they need and reclaim the deposit on a clean close, paying once. Sybils cannot pool deposits: each puppet must win and fund its own slot-lock with no bulk discount, so N identities cost N deposits, growing linearly. A sparrow-scale penalty confiscates deposits tied to double-signing in a slot, so marginal cost per extra identity stays unavoidable while honest users pay once.
